Maria P.: Quick follow-up from the modularization RFC — can we agree on the tradeoffs between strict cohesion (one service = one capability) vs. composable facets for the runtime hot path?

Ashwin: Short answer: we need both, but different surface areas. Hot path needs tiny, cohesive pieces for latency. Control/telemetry can be composable.

Devon: Agreed. Main worry is owner churn if we split too many tiny services — coordination cost spikes.

Sloane: Also deployment complexity. If each facet has independent deploys, we need stronger contracts and automated compatibility checks.

Maria P.: Right — here's a concrete proposal: split runtime into 3 facets: request-routing (placement + policy), execution-core (inference runtime + KV cache), and telemetry/control (tracing, rollout, metrics). Each facet has a minimal public contract.

Elaine: That seems reasonable. How do we handle the KV cache ownership? It's heavily touched by the execution core and session mesh today.

Ashwin: Proposal: execution-core owns physical KV cache and cache semantics. Request-router can reference cache via a thin adapter API (GetPrefix, WarmKV, Invalidate). Keep adapter stable.

Devon: Will adapters add extra RPC latency? need numbers.

Sloane: We can co-locate router and adapter on the same node for hot-paths initially to reduce hop cost, then split later.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary cluster created: modular-slice-canary-01 (image: rwinf-runtime:vnext).

Maria P.: For tech debt paydown, I want a phased migration with debt buckets: 
- Phase 0: extract adapter surfaces and compile interface tests (no runtime split)
- Phase 1: deploy adapter + co-location on canary; shadow traffic for 2 weeks
- Phase 2: enable real routing and observe latency/throughput deltas
- Phase 3: roll full split with rollback path to old monolith

Ashwin: Important: automated contract test must run in CI and premerge, including golden KV semantics test and prefix eviction invariants.

Devon: Suggestion: add a "latency-safety" gate that blocks any change widening P99 by >5ms on hot-path synthetic.

Sloane: Also add a gradual rollout plan per region, not global. Our EU cluster has different memory pressure patterns.

Elaine: Who's oncall for the canary? we should assign runbooks now.

Maria P.: Volunteers: @Ashwin for phase 0/1 lead, @Devon for performance measurement, @Sloane for rollout orchestration. Elaine will author the runbook. I'll own design docs and RFC update.

Ashwin: I'll start by extracting the adapter interface into pkg/kv/adapter and add a mock impl. Will open a small PR to start the CI contracts.

Devon: I'll set up a perf harness that hits the co-located adapter path and compare to current monolith. Need sample traffic profile.

Sloane: I'll capture rollout steps in the runbook: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated abort on error rates or latency regressions.

Maria P.: Edge cases: we must support mixed-mode where some tenants use old monolith and some use new split. Routing policy must be tenant-aware.

Ashwin: Tenant-aware routing implies request-router needs a lightweight tenant map service. We can keep it as an in-memory shard initially and make it eventually consistent via CDC.

Devon: Concern: CDC lag might cause misrouting. Add fallback: if tenant not found, route to monolith.

Sloane: Good rollback pattern. Also add detailed logs for any fallback routing — high cardinality but only in canary mode.

Elaine: Runbook checklist (draft):
- Prechecks: CI contracts green, perf baseline captured, canary cluster ready
- Canary: co-locate adapter, shadow traffic for 2 weeks, verify correctness metrics
- Promote: enable routing for 1% tenants, monitor 24h, escalate if >0.5% error or P99 regress >5ms
- Rollback: toggle router to monolith routing, drain new pods, revert commits if needed

Maria P.: Ok. Next steps: Ashwin opens the adapter extraction PR by EOD Thu, Devon posts perf harness results within 5 days, Sloane drafts the rollout checklist by Monday. Elaine will create the runbook doc and link here.

Ashwin: ack.

Devon: ack, will capture both mean and tail numbers.

Sloane: ack, will include region-specific thresholds.

Elaine: I'll create the runbook: /docs/runbooks/split-runtime-relink.md and drop link when ready.

Maria P.: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the PR land and initial perf runs. If anyone finds a blocker, ping me directly. :thumbsup:

Devon: one small note — let's add a postmortem checkbox to the plan even if everything goes fine, to capture lessons and remaining debt.

Maria P.: Good call. Added to plan.
